summary: Intermittent runner impersonation denied after Okta claim sanitization
summary_detail: Several internal support tooling runs (runner service) are intermittently returning 403 when attempting to impersonate user sessions. The denial correlates with recent Okta claim sanitization rollout that strips non-ASCII characters and truncates long group attributes.
description:
Issue summary:
- After the Okta claim sanitization rollout (2026-03-08), service-runner impersonation attempts intermittently receive 403 Forbidden from the internal console authorization layer.

Impact:
- On-call engineers are unable to assume affected user sessions to run elevated runbooks ~15-30% of attempts during peak hours.
- Affects internal incident response and automated remediation flows for a subset of service accounts that have legacy group attributes.

Environment:
- Prod, us-west-2. Observed across multiple clusters and proxies; not present in staging.

Observed behavior:
- Impersonation calls return 403 with "rbac:role-claim-mismatch" and an empty roles array in the authorization debug payload.

Expected behavior:
- Impersonation should succeed when requester has delegated runbook role and claim mapping is intact.

Business urgency:
- P1 (Sev1) - Blocks critical runbook execution during incidents. Needs mitigation and rollback plan if needed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use service-runner to start impersonation: POST /api/v1/impersonate with X-Run-As header set to target user
2) Observe 403 response in ~1/5 attempts during peak; success rate varies by target identity
3) Capture debug headers: x-auth-debug shows 'roles: []' and 'claim-normalization: stripped_nonascii'
4) Compare Okta SAML assertion raw vs identity-proxy after sanitization: group claim truncated to 256 chars and non-ASCII removed
logs: 2026-03-11T13:22:14Z ERROR authz: rbcauthorizer.go:182 - authorization failed: rbcauthorizer: role claim mismatch (user: svc-deployer-legacy) request_id=8f3a2e
nginx-proxy: 403 response for /api/v1/impersonate request_id=8f3a2e upstream_status=200 auth_status=403
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10): Filed after two oncall reports. Suspect correlation with claim sanitization rollout on 2026-03-08.
Ravi Patel (2026-03-10): Reproduced locally by replaying SAML assertion through identity-proxy. Confirmed truncation + character removal. Adding SRE and IAM to investigate mappings.
SRE - Jordan Blake (2026-03-11): Observed similar failures in autoscaling runbook queue. Rate ~18% denial for accounts with long composite group lists.

IAM - Lila Ortiz (2026-03-11): Okta team confirms sanitization policy v1 deployed; policy strips non-ASCII and truncates attributes >256 chars. We're checking claim->role mapping service for unexpected key drops.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Claim truncation cuts off role-mapping sentinel suffix, causing mapper to not recognize delegated groups.
Hypothesis B: Non-ASCII removal mutates legacy group IDs that contained accented characters, causing exact-match RBAC lookups to fail.
Mapped flow: Okta SAML -> identity-proxy sanitization -> internal-identity-service -> role-mapper -> console authz. Break appears between sanitization and role-mapper matching.
Test: Replayed raw SAML with and without sanitization through role-mapper; sanitized input failed to map delegated roles in 100% of test cases where sentinel suffix truncated.
Cross-reference: Related to INT-224466 (ephemeral-cli-token-chain-rotation) - not a direct duplicate but similar claim-handling code paths.
Observed frequency: spikes during scheduled group syncs when some identities accumulate long group lists; correlated with sync window 02:00-04:00 UTC.
mitigation_plan: 1) Short-term: Add auth proxy feature flag to bypass sanitization for delegated-runbook assertions (feature_flag "skip_sanitize_delegation") and roll back to 100% success for impersonation until role-mapper fix ships.
2) Medium-term: Update role-mapper to perform fuzzy/normalized matching and accept legacy variants (PR #622), with unit tests for truncated-suffix and non-ascii removal.
3) Long-term: Update Okta group hygiene and establish pre-sync validation to avoid attribute lists >256 chars.
next_steps: A. Run feature-flag canary in us-west-2 today (2026-03-12) targeting runner-service traffic only
B. Monitor impersonation success rate and logs for request_id correlation; rollback flag if side-effects observed
C. Coordinate with Okta team to schedule a controlled fix and post-mortem documenting sanitization impacts
estimated_impact_reduction: Canary expected to reduce impersonation denials to <1% for affected flows; full role-mapper fix will eliminate regressions for legacy group names.
resolution: IN PROGRESS - feature-flagging plan approved. Canaries scheduled 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. Role-mapper PR under review; target merge 2026-03-14. Final resolution pending after role-mapper deployment and Okta sync verification.
notes: Do not escalate to customer-facing incident yet; internal runbook execution impacted only. If P1 persists after canary, prepare rollback of sanitization policy and notify leadership.
